In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endovascular thrombolysis has been proven to be a safe and effective treatment for selected patients with acute ischemic stroke and is the standard of care in this population.

there is no single best treatment, but a combination of different approaches is the most promising strategy to improve the efficacy of endovascular recalanization in the era of mechanical thrombectomy.

the future of endovascular treatment for stroke will include the use of novel and more effective devices and the combination of these with adjunct therapies that enhance recanalization and improve collateral perfusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is room for improvement in the treatment of stroke patients.

the combination of mechanical thrombectomy with other approaches, such as the use of thrombolytics, thrombectomy devices, and neuroprotectants, may be a promising way to improve reperfusion therapy and expand the number of patients eligible for thrombectomy.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the future of acute stroke care is a multimodal approach that combines endovascular thrombolysis with pharmacotherapy to improve reperfusion and collateral circulation, and to prevent secondary brain injury.

there is a clear need to develop new approaches to expand the number of eligible patients for endovascular treatment and to improve the effectiveness of current treatments by combining them with approaches that enhance collateral perfusion.
the future of stroke care lies in a combination of approaches that will improve the effectiveness of recanalization and expand treatment to patients with poor imaging results.
